title: DreamShader
description: DreamShader turns text into Unreal materials. A .dss source is HLSL with declarations. Its uniforms become material parameters, and its export function becomes the material or a material function. A .dsi makes a material instance. A .dsp makes a Custom Pass render pipeline (UE 5.8). A .dsh holds shared helpers. .dsm and .dsf are the older 1.x language. Sources live in the project's DShader/ folder, and each one builds assets at the same path under /Game. Use this tool to check, compile and preview sources, read their errors, look up the nodes a source can call, and turn an existing material back into text. Read the language reference before you write a source.

actions.name: check
actions.description: Check a source for errors. It builds nothing and writes nothing. Run it after every edit: it is the fastest test.

file.description: Source path relative to the project root, e.g. DShader/UI/M_Panel.dss

all.description: Check every source of the project instead of one file

actions.name: compile
actions.description: Build the assets a source makes, such as a material. In the user's editor, a material of the default kind stays in memory until the user saves it. In a host, every asset is saved to disk. With shaders=true it also compiles the shaders and reports their errors at source lines; then it always saves.

file.description: Source path relative to the project root

force.description: Rebuild even when the source has not changed

shaders.description: Also compile the shaders and report their errors

actions.name: diagnostics
actions.description: List the errors and warnings from the last check or compile. It compiles nothing. Without file, it lists every file that has some, with a count for each.

file.description: Source path relative to the project root

actions.name: lookup
actions.description: Find a node a source can call: the UE.* and Substrate.* nodes, and material attributes such as m.BaseColor. An exact name returns its inputs, outputs and properties. Part of a name returns the names that contain it.

name.description: A node or attribute name, or part of one: UE.TextureSample, Lerp, BaseColor

actions.name: preview
actions.description: Render a material source to a PNG and measure the picture. It compiles the source first, as compile does in the editor. The result says what the image shows: how much of the mesh is visible or see-through, the mean colour, the brightness, and how much is near white or near black. With frames, it renders several moments side by side, to show an animation.

file.description: A .dss, .dsi or .dsm path relative to the project root

mesh.description: Preview mesh; default sphere. UI materials always draw on a plane

width.description: Width of one frame in pixels; default 512, or 256 with frames

height.description: Height in pixels; default 512, or 256 with frames

yaw.description: Camera orbit yaw in degrees; default -157.5

pitch.description: Camera orbit pitch in degrees; default -11.25

force.description: Recompile even when the source has not changed

time.description: The material's Time in seconds, for the first frame; default 0

frames.description: How many frames to render side by side, spread evenly over duration; default 1. The strip is at most 8192 pixels wide

duration.description: Seconds the frames cover, starting at time; default 1. One period of the animation shows all of it

tone.description: How colour reaches the image. editor (default): the project's exposure and the filmic tone curve, as the editor shows it; bright colours drift toward white. fixed: the same at exposure 1. linear: exposure 1 and no tone curve, so a pixel shows the output value, clipped at 1

actions.name: info
actions.description: Report the plugin and engine versions, the source folders, the default backend, and what this engine process can do: editor or host, renders or not.

actions.name: decompile
actions.description: Turn an existing material, material function or material instance into a DreamShader source (.dss, .dsi or .dsp). It writes a source file, never an asset.

out.description: Destination relative to the project root; default under DShader/Decompiled/

readable.description: Prefer HLSL operators over exact node calls (a rebuild may then use other node classes)

overwrite.description: Replace the destination when it exists
